recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. The current build-scope source already conveys the WG decision and later compatible terminology updates; adding more prose would be redundant.
issue_request: FHIR-36347 was Published/Persuasive for R5 and requested reconciliation of conflicting HTTP and Search page rules for allowed search parameters in base searches, especially avoiding a requirement that multi-type search parameters share the same SearchParameter.base definition.
initial_application: Commit d16636ba8132d2c4141090668e222c1e74b717a9 explicitly applied FHIR-36347 by removing the HTTP page's local SearchParameter.base-only restriction, linking HTTP Variant Searches to the Search page, and expanding the Search page's no-type, single-type, and multi-type parameter rules.
additional_context: FHIR-I minutes from 2022-03-21 confirm the Persuasive 13-0-0 motion. Later FHIR-34866 work added SearchParameter.alias wording to the same Search page guidance without changing the FHIR-36347 rule, and a later FHIR-39010 Zulip thread quoted the R5 clarification as operative guidance.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/http.html now delegates parameter availability for multiple-type and all-type base searches to search.html#type, while source/search.html states that no _type uses all-resource base parameters, one _type uses that resource's parameters, and multiple _type values may use commonly referenced server names based on SearchParameter.code or alias.

related_jiras.note: Added SearchParameter.alias/aliasCode terminology to the same Search page rule without changing the FHIR-36347 policy.
A later package-artifact discussion quoted the R5 multiple-resource-type search clarification; this issue was already represented on the combined branch.
